content: Hydroxychloroquine belongs to a class of medications known as antimalarials. It is prescribed to prevent and treat acute malaria attacks. Additionally, it is used to manage discoid or systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis in patients whose symptoms have not improved with other treatments. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other conditions; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Hydroxychloroquine is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For malaria prevention in adults, the usual dosage is two tablets taken once a week on the same day each week. The first dose should be taken 1–2 weeks before traveling to a malaria-endemic area, and the regimen should continue for 8 weeks after exposure. For treating acute malaria attacks in adults, the typical dosage involves taking four tablets immediately, followed by two tablets 6–8 hours later, and then two tablets daily for the next two days. For infants and children, the dosage is determined based on the child’s weight, and your doctor will calculate the appropriate amount. For lupus erythematosus, the usual dosage is one or two tablets taken once or twice daily. For rheumatoid arthritis, the typical dosage is one to three tablets taken once daily. To minimize stomach upset, hydroxychloroquine can be taken with a glass of milk or a meal. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take hydroxychloroquine exactly as directed, without altering the dosage or frequency unless advised by your doctor. If you are taking hydroxychloroquine for rheumatoid arthritis, you should notice symptom improvement within 6 months. If your symptoms do not improve or worsen, discontinue the medication and contact your doctor. Once you and your doctor confirm that the medication is effective, do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, as rheumatoid arthritis symptoms may return if the medication is discontinued. Hydroxychloroquine is occasionally used to treat porphyria cutanea tarda. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Before starting hydroxychloroquine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine (Aralen), primaquine, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs you are taking, especially acetaminophen (Tylenol), digoxin (Lanoxin), iron-containing medications (including multivitamins), isoniazid (Nydrazid), methotrexate (Rheumatrex), niacin, rifampin (Rifadin, Rimactane), and any vitamins or herbal products. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had liver disease, psoriasis, porphyria or other blood disorders, G6PD deficiency, dermatitis, or if you consume large amounts of alcohol. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have experienced vision changes while taking hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine, or primaquine. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking hydroxychloroquine, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: headache, dizziness, loss of appetite, upset stomach, diarrhea, stomach pain, vomiting, or skin rash. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: difficulty reading or seeing (e.g., missing words, letters, or parts of objects), sensitivity to light, blurred distance vision, seeing light flashes or streaks, hearing difficulties, ringing in the ears, muscle weakness, skin bleeding or bruising, hair bleaching or loss, mood or mental changes, irregular heartbeat, drowsiness, or seizures. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store hydroxychloroquine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Children are particularly sensitive to hydroxychloroquine overdoses, so ensure the medication is kept out of their reach. Children should not use hydroxychloroquine for long-term therapy. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to the medication. If you are taking hydroxychloroquine for an extended period, regular eye exams are essential due to the risk of serious vision problems. If you notice any changes in vision, stop taking hydroxychloroquine and contact your doctor immediately. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
